title: The Palms concert, mouthpiece ridges and daily practice
summary: Details of The Palms concert, the ridges on his mouthpiece for triple tonguing, and his daily scales.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Is that the one by the composer? I remember a piece called The Palms by Fauré.
Do you think that's the one?
The Palms. That they use on Easter Sunday.

That's the one. And it was accompanied by Jenny Jasmine and sponsored by Walter De Silva. Walter De Silva. He used to sponsor quite a bit of concerts in those days. And the concert, the one concert with Ann that have a dance. And then he would play the dance with everybody, broken horn. That's the thing that tickled me. And then he had a file, a round file. And he used to get his mouthpiece made, room walls. But it wasn't shaped. The cup wasn't shaped like the others, you know. It was deep because his mouth was very small. And the mouthpiece had to be very small, so he had made the order. And then he'd file that hole. And then he'd go right in there and keep for hours at the time. And then he'd have the horn there. He'd try to put the mouthpiece on. It wasn't satisfied. He'd go back again, file it again. Then he'd put some ridges on the top of the mouthpiece. Oh, ridges. Yeah, you know, just three ridges on the mouthpiece. I did ask him why did he do that. He said, oh, when I have a triple tongue, that's a big help.
But I keep from slipping when he tripled down. Yeah. And four, so Christ keep it. Yeah. Right across the...
They have three, you see, they're round like this. He put one like this and one like that. And then you file that, you know.
Equally spaced. Yeah. File. No, that's strange to me.

Isn't it strange? Mm-hmm. And he never put his mouthpiece down. It was always in his pocket. Yeah. Whether he played or not, he kept it in his pocket. Well, he believed in that mouthpiece. I was telling you how he used to practice.
To practice. I know other common players ever do that.

Every evening before he'd leave, he'd run his scales. Mm-hmm. And run water in his home. Yeah, always run water in his home. And he'd throw it out before he leaves. Mm-hmm. One time he was very, very sick. You remember when he played for the... For almost this day of the year. Mm-hmm. The first time he went out. Mm-hmm. As weak as he could be. A man came and told him that he had a job. That he said they had a parade. But he didn't have no qual된 stuff. Mm-hmm.
